FEATURE / WORLD TOPOLOGY / WORLDBUILDER ISSUE: Establish the first top-down macro-world generation pass for the real game, using `KentridgePlayableSlice` as the initial playable anchor. The goal is to stop treating Kentridge as an isolated local showcase and begin defining the actual Mounting Force world from the top down: major settlements/regions, their relative placement, and—most importantly—the travel/topology relationships that connect them.

This is a REFERENCE-DRIVEN LAYOUT task, not a town art-direction task. Do not spend this issue defining the visual style, material palette, architecture language, building details, or decorative theme of Kentridge, Hightown, Moordell, Rossdam, Fairy Village, Orc Village, or any other settlement. Those concerns belong to separate worldbuilding/style work. Here, a settlement needs enough generated spatial presence to prove where it is, how large its reserved envelope is, how the player approaches/leaves it, and how it connects to the rest of the world.

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES / EVIDENCE PRECEDENCE:
1. Inspect the original `jlashmet/mounting-force` repository, especially branch `agent/original-world-content-inventory`. Use the source-derived `docs/world-story-graph.yaml`, `docs/world-progression-chains.yaml`, `docs/world-generator-level-contracts.yaml`, original `Art/overworld*.tmx` / relevant town maps, and the actual Warp/Portal/scripted transition implementations to establish hard traversal and progression topology. Do not infer a required route from visual proximity alone when the original runtime proves otherwise.
2. Inspect the imported voxel references under `References/MountingForce/`, especially `contracts/world-progression-handoff.yaml`, `guidance/world-inferred-geography.yaml`, `guidance/world-procgen-clusters.yaml`, `SOURCE_MANIFEST.yaml`, and any relevant contracts. The imported handoff explicitly distinguishes verified hard rules from inferred guidance; preserve that distinction in the new world model.
3. Inspect the old map screenshots under `References/MountingForce/map-images/` and the available story/world-description reference material. Use these to understand recognizable macro shapes, approach directions, adjacency, terrain corridors, and how the old maps relate spatially. Screenshots are evidence for composition/orientation, not a requirement to copy old tile coordinates.
4. When the imported handoff is incomplete, go back to the original `mounting-force` source rather than guessing. Record provenance for any important topology/placement decision.

TOP-DOWN WORLD MODEL:
Create or extend a reusable WorldBuilder-level macro layout representation for the actual game world. It should be able to describe major named places/regions, settlement envelopes, entrances/exits, travel corridors, and connections separately from their eventual detailed architecture. Connections must be able to distinguish hard/verified topology from soft placement guidance so later procedural layout work can move or reshape geography without breaking story reachability.

Start from Kentridge because `KentridgePlayableSlice` is the current playable slice, but solve enough of the surrounding/global graph that Kentridge's exits are not arbitrary dead ends. Identify the major legacy destinations and intermediary regions from the source rather than relying on a hard-coded list from this ticket. Reserve/place them in approximately the same world relationships as the old game where evidence supports that, and preserve the same meaningful ways of getting from one place to another: which route/corridor/region leads to which destination, which approaches are connected, and which required progression paths must remain possible. Exact distances, tile coordinates, rotations, and map dimensions may change substantially for a modern 3D voxel world.

For inferred geography, treat direction/sign/dialogue hints as soft scoring evidence, not hard truth. For example, the imported geography guidance contains local-map directional hints among Kentridge, Hightown, Moordell, Rossdam, Stanley's house, forest, graveyard, Fairy Village, and Orc Village; use those when they are compatible with verified transitions, but never let an inferred north/west/east relationship invalidate an authoritative route. The topology must win over cosmetic compass fidelity.

WORLD GENERATION BOUNDARY: The macro layout, region reservation, settlement placement, entrances/exits, and connecting routes must be produced through the standard WorldBuilder/shared world-authoring path. `KentridgePlayableSlice` may select the Mounting Force world definition, seed, scale, and starting location, but it must not own bespoke direct voxel-writing, one-off procedural mesh code, or hand-authored world coordinates in the `.unity` hierarchy. If the shared WorldBuilder cannot currently express named regions, world-scale connectivity, path/corridor constraints, reserved settlement envelopes, terrain-aware route solving, or deterministic placement from a semantic world graph, add those as reusable engine/worldbuilding capabilities instead of solving them only inside Kentridge.

The generated result does NOT need final town buildings for every location in this issue. It may use intentionally simple neutral settlement envelopes/grounded markers/low-detail reserved footprints for non-Kentridge destinations when necessary to make the macro layout inspectable, provided those are clearly treated as layout instrumentation rather than claimed final art. The actual terrain and travel corridors used to validate the world should be legitimate WorldBuilder output, walkable where applicable, and free of obvious impossible slopes/intersections. Do not allow temporary markers to become the permanent architecture implementation.

PRESERVE GAME SEMANTICS: The original handoff requires verified scene/progression dependencies to remain satisfiable even when geometry moves. Solve physical traversal together with those dependencies. Do not invent prerequisites for isolated content, and do not convert negative guards or actor-state prerequisites into fake geography. A modern continuous or differently partitioned world is acceptable; identical old scene boundaries are not required. What must survive is the meaningful reachability/topology and progression intent.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) `KentridgePlayableSlice` is driven by a reusable Mounting Force macro-world definition through the production WorldBuilder path rather than an isolated set of scene-local coordinates.
(2) The macro model represents all major legacy settlements/destinations and the intermediary regions/routes needed to reproduce the source-proven world connectivity; the implementation records the source/provenance used for each hard connection and important soft placement relationship.
(3) Every verified legacy traversal/transition relationship relevant to the represented world remains satisfiable in the generated layout. Required story/progression paths are not broken by procedural placement.
(4) Kentridge is a real anchor in that larger layout: its exits/routes lead into generated world corridors that resolve toward the appropriate neighboring/next regions rather than arbitrary dead ends or showcase boundaries.
(5) Relative placement and approach directions follow the old map screenshots/TMX/sign/dialogue guidance where reasonably supported, while hard runtime topology takes precedence over inferred compass orientation. This is not a tile-for-tile or coordinate-for-coordinate remake.
(6) Town/settlement style, materials, architecture detail, and decorative identity are explicitly out of scope. The issue should not duplicate the separate town-architecture showcase work.
(7) Macro layout and routing are deterministic for a fixed seed and expressed through reusable WorldBuilder/shared-system concepts. Scene code only selects/composes semantic intent.
(8) Focused behavioral regressions exercise the production world-generation path and verify the world graph, deterministic placement, required route connectivity/reachability, and Kentridge's connection into the larger graph. Include failure cases proving a placement cannot silently sever a hard route.
(9) Produce inspectable runtime evidence of the generated top-down world layout (for example a debug/top-down view plus normal playable traversal evidence) and compare it against the legacy screenshots/source topology. Semantic graph tests alone are not sufficient to prove the resulting geography is coherent.
(10) The exact built-application `KentridgePlayableSlice` harness reaches a usable rendered scene without startup/runtime exceptions, and the generated surrounding world/routes can be inspected from the built player.
(11) Check blast radius and cost of any new world-scale solver/representation: world-build time, memory, chunk/voxel generation, path solving, and any effect on existing showcase/game scenes. Do not weaken existing device budgets.

NON-GOALS: final town architecture; per-town palettes/materials; exact reproduction of old pixel-map coordinates; final population/NPC placement except where a hard story/traversal anchor is needed to validate topology; rewriting story progression; or hand-authoring a giant static scene as a substitute for WorldBuilder.
resolutionSummary: Added a reusable source-backed Mounting Force macro-world model and deterministic WorldBuilder planner with verified-vs-inferred provenance, reserved destination envelopes, hard-route reachability constraints, and shared terrain-grounded voxel corridors/markers. Kentridge now selects this production world definition without scene-local voxel writing, and exact built-player evidence validates the post-load top-down layout plus real CharacterMotor traversal.
